final_message:
I reproduced it on Linux by simulating Windows path handling. The repro is `repro/cross-drive-ignore.js`. It loads ESLint first, then replaces the functions on the shared `node:path` module with their `path.win32` versions and sets the cwd to `C:\Project`. It needs no Windows files because the code is passed in as text. I haven't run it on a real Windows machine.

Run: `node repro/cross-drive-ignore.js` (exits 1 while the bug is present)

```
path.relative("C:\\Project", "F:\\foo.js") = "F:\\foo.js"
OK   C:\Project\foo.js (inside cwd)               getConfigStatus: matched;  Linter/ESLint lint it
OK   C:\other\foo.js (same drive, outside cwd)    getConfigStatus: external; Linter: "No matching configuration found", ESLint: "File ignored because outside of base path."
FAIL F:\foo.js (different drive)                  getConfigStatus: matched;  Linter#verify, ESLint#lintText -> no-undef; isPathIgnored: false
```

**Likely cause:** In `@eslint/config-array` 0.18.0, `ConfigArray#getConfigWithStatus` (`node_modules/@eslint/config-array/dist/cjs/index.cjs`, around line 953) decides whether a file is outside the base path like this:

```js
const relativeFilePath = path.relative(this.basePath, filePath);
if (relativeFilePath.startsWith("..")) { /* external */ }
```

On Windows, `path.relative` returns the target path unchanged when it is on a different drive. That gives `"F:\\foo.js"`, which doesn't start with `..`, so the file counts as inside the base path. With no ignore pattern matching it, the file gets linted. The same `startsWith("..")` check is also in `shouldIgnorePath` and `isDirectoryIgnored`.

This explains why both the `Linter` class (base path is the cwd, see `lib/linter/linter.js`) and the `ESLint` class/CLI are affected. In the repro, the `C:\other\foo.js` case shows the check works for a file on the same drive.
